ops.name: auth.totpBegin
ops.outputType: { secret: string; uri: string; qrSvg: string }

ops.name: import.assistStatus
ops.outputType: { kind: 'check' | 'pdf'; running: boolean; startedAt: number; groupsDone: number; groupsTotal: number; partsTotal: number; error: string | null } | null

ops.name: networth.summary
ops.description: Net worth now (assets minus debts, in the main currency), each account with its value and, for investments with recorded values, the gain, plus net worth at the end of each month. months: how many months of history (0 = all).

ops.name: valuations.list
ops.description: Recorded values of an account (e.g. an investment portfolio), newest first.

ops.name: valuations.set
ops.description: Record what an account (e.g. a broker portfolio or savings plan) was worth on a date, in cents of the account currency. Payments after that date are added on top until the next value.

ops.name: balances.list
ops.description: Balances the bank showed for an account (end of day), newest first, each compared with what Kasboek expected from the one before: a difference means a missing or doubled transaction.

ops.name: balances.set
ops.description: Record the balance the bank shows for an account at the end of a day (today or earlier), in cents of the account currency. The account balance is then counted from it. Returns what Kasboek expected and the difference.

ops.name: summary.year
ops.description: One year: income and spending per month and per category (main currency, transfers left out), and totals for every year with data.

ops.name: fx.status
ops.description: Currencies in use and the exchange rates Kasboek has for them (units per 1 euro). Totals are shown in the main currency.

ops.name: fx.rates
ops.description: Exchange rates typed in by hand, newest first (units of the currency per 1 euro).

ops.name: fx.setRate
ops.description: Set an exchange rate by hand: how many units of `currency` one euro was worth on `date`. Used from that date on, until the next rate.

ops.name: accounts.list
ops.description: List bank accounts with their current balance (cents).

ops.name: categories.list
ops.description: List all categories (id, name, kind: expense/income/transfer).

ops.name: categories.create
ops.description: Create a new category.

ops.name: transactions.list
ops.description: Search transactions. Amounts are integer cents: negative = money out, positive = money in. Filter by account, category (or "none" for uncategorised), month (YYYY-MM), date range, free-text search or direction. Returns a page plus totals for the whole filter.

ops.name: transactions.edit
ops.description: Fix one transaction: its category, notes, readable description or counterparty name. Dates and amounts can only be changed by the person.

ops.name: transactions.splits
ops.description: The parts of a split transaction (empty when it isn’t split).

ops.name: transactions.split
ops.description: Split one transaction over categories (e.g. a receipt with groceries and household). The parts’ amountCents must add up to the transaction’s amount (same sign as the transaction). An empty list removes the split.

ops.name: transactions.rename
ops.description: Give several transactions the same readable counterparty name (e.g. all "CRF MKT BRUGGE" rows → "Carrefour"). The bank’s own text is kept.

ops.name: transactions.categorize
ops.description: Set the category of one or more transactions (categoryId null = uncategorised).

ops.name: goals.list
ops.description: Savings goals: target amount and date, how much is saved (an account’s balance or an amount kept by hand), what is left, and what to put aside per month to reach it by the date. Main currency, cents.

ops.name: goals.create
ops.description: Create a savings goal: a name, a target in cents of the main currency, optionally a date (YYYY-MM-DD), and either an account whose balance counts as saved, or an amount saved so far.

ops.name: memory.remember
ops.description: Remember a lasting fact or preference for later conversations: one short sentence (max 300 characters) in the person’s language. No account or card numbers, passwords, or amounts you can look up.

ops.name: memory.forget
ops.description: Forget remembered items, by the ids shown in brackets in your memory.

ops.name: alerts.list
ops.description: Warnings now: budgets at 80% or more this month, and current accounts whose balance would go below zero before the next income (counting fixed costs still due).

ops.name: summary.review
ops.description: Facts for a review of one month (YYYY-MM): income and spending against the average of the three months before, each spending category against its average (biggest change first), budgets that went over, and payments that stand out (far above what that payee usually costs, or a large first payment). All in cents of the main currency.

ops.name: insights.get
ops.description: Tips for the Overview found locally from the data of one month (YYYY-MM). Not offered to the assistant.

ops.name: insights.feedback
ops.description: Remember on this computer what the person did with a tip (hidden, not useful, useful). Never synced.

ops.name: insights.preview
ops.description: The exact text that would be sent to the assistant to write tips for one month. Not offered to the assistant.

ops.name: insights.run
ops.description: Have the assistant write tips for one month from the local facts; consent: true records the person’s agreement for this provider. Not offered to the assistant.

ops.name: insights.cancel
ops.description: Stop the assistant while it writes tips.

ops.name: insights.status
ops.description: Whether the assistant is writing tips now, for which month and since when. Not offered to the assistant.
ops.outputType: { running: boolean; month: string | null; startedAt: string | null }

ops.name: insights.restoreDismissed
ops.description: Show the tips the person hid on this computer again.

ops.name: recurring.list
ops.description: Payments and income that come back at a steady rhythm (subscriptions, rent, insurance, energy, salary), found from the last 14 months: usual amount, rhythm, last and next date, whether it is paid, due or late this month, and price changes. Plus fixed costs per month and what is still due this month.

ops.name: recurring.hide
ops.description: Stop counting a detected fixed cost or fixed income (by its key from recurring_list) when the person says it is not fixed, or count it again with hidden: false. Hidden items are left out of fixed-cost totals and balance warnings; transactions are not changed.

ops.name: transfers.find
ops.description: Transfers between the person’s own accounts that aren’t paired yet: money out of one account and into another within 3 days, the same amount, or between currencies its value at that day’s rate minus the bank’s cost. confidence "iban" means the account number matches (sure); "amount" only the amount and date. costCents: between currencies, the exchange cost in the sending account’s currency.

ops.name: transfers.pair
ops.description: Pair transfers between own accounts (from transfers_find). Both halves go into a transfer category, so they count as neither income nor spending. Between currencies, the exchange cost (costCents, or worked out from the rate) is booked as a fee on the sending half.

ops.name: transfers.cost
ops.outputType: { cross: boolean; currency: string | null; costCents: number | null }

ops.name: transfers.setCost
ops.description: Change the exchange cost of a paired transfer between currencies (e.g. the exact cost from the bank statement), in cents of the sending account’s currency. Either half’s id.

ops.name: rules.list
ops.description: List categorisation rules ("text in counterparty/description → category").

ops.name: rules.create
ops.description: Create a rule that puts transactions whose counterparty and/or description matches `pattern` (case-insensitive) into a category. match: contains (anywhere, default), word (as a whole word) or starts (at the start); texts shorter than 4 characters always match as a whole word. field iban: pattern is the counterparty’s account number, matched exactly (good for transfers to the person’s own accounts). New imports use it; applyToExisting also categorises uncategorised transactions now. Check first with rules_preview.

ops.name: rules.preview
ops.description: Shows what a rule would match before creating it: how many transactions, how many are uncategorised, how many already sit in another category, and a few examples.

ops.name: rules.update
ops.description: Change a rule (its text, where it looks, how it matches, or its category). applyToExisting also categorises uncategorised transactions it now matches.

ops.name: rules.delete
ops.description: Delete a rule. Transactions it already categorised keep their category.

ops.name: budgets.list
ops.description: Budgets and spending per spending category for a month (cents).

ops.name: budgets.set
ops.description: Set (or clear with null) the monthly budget for a spending category, in cents.

ops.name: import.current
ops.description: The CSV import the person has open: detected bank, column mapping, totals and every row with its status (ready / duplicate / problem / skipped), issues and category. Returns null when no import is open.

ops.name: import.raw
ops.description: Raw cells of the open CSV import (header row, any info lines above it, and a window of data rows by index). Use it to understand the file before changing the mapping.
ops.outputType: { headerRow: number; header: string[]; rows: { index: number; cells: string[] }[]; totalRows: number; preamble: string[][] }

ops.name: import.remap
ops.description: Change the column mapping of the open import: zero-based column indexes, headerRow (index of the header line in the file), dateOrder (DMY/YMD/MDY), decimal mark, invertSign. Nothing is saved until the import is committed.

ops.name: import.updateRows
ops.description: Fix rows of the open import before it is saved: set a category, correct a date (YYYY-MM-DD), amount (cents) or description, include a duplicate on purpose, or skip a row. Add a short note saying why. Nothing is saved until commit.

ops.name: import.commit
ops.description: Save the ready rows of the open import as transactions. Only after the person has reviewed the preview.

ops.name: import.checkApply
ops.outputType: { preview: ImportPreview; rules: number; categorised: number; skipped: number }

ops.name: summary.month
ops.description: Income, spending, budget left, spending per category and the last 6 months, for one month (cents).
